scope: Corollary 7.6 (Retained scalar tests) of the manuscript “Koebe's Circle-Domain Conjecture” (preprints/Koebes-Circle-Domain-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 071 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 f0080bd36e38b2cd), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 60-61. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let G ⊂ b C contain infinity, let X = G ∪ B be its quotient sphere, and fix R with {|z| ≥ R} ∪ {∞} ⊂ G. Let u1, . . . , um ∈ C(X, R) be smooth on G, with R G |dui|2 < ∞, and suppose area (ui, uj)(B)  = 0 (i ̸= j). (7.18) For every positive sequence εn → 0 there are finite bordered completions (Qn, gn), nested smooth cores Kn ⊂ G containing every compact subset of G in their interiors eventually, normalized conformal maps fn : Q◦ n → Ωn onto finite circle domains, and smooth real tests vi,n on Ωn such that vi,n ◦ fn = ui near Kn, (7.19) m X i=1 Z Ωn\fn(Kn) |∇vi,n|2 da < ε2 n, (7.20) X T Ai,n(T)2 < ε2 n (1 ≤ i ≤ m). (7.21) 60 Here T ranges over the complementary round disks of Ωn; the cluster values of vi,n at T lie in an interval of length Ai,n(T). The metric gn is the original metric near Kn. After passage to a subsequence, fn → f locally uniformly on G, where f is normalized and univalent and f(G) is a circle domain. All finite target holes lie in |w| < 5R. The source-contour retention, correspondence, and bounds of Theorem 7.5(iv) also hold. In particular, these conclusions allow arbitrarily many, and possibly uncountably many, point components in the limiting complement.
